Subject: Proposal: 3yr Prepay + Milestone Billing & Net90 Exception

Hi Janet —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is Redwood's proposed commitment schedule for the 3-year prepay (covers hosted API + dedicated burst capacity) along with an initial SOW appendix that maps usage ramp to milestone invoicing. Key points: 

- Total committed spend: $2,700,000 over 36 months (annualized $900k)
- Suggested billing: 30% upfront at signature, then 3 milestone invoices per year tied to defined usage bands (see SOW tab)
- Recommended term discount: 20% off public list for multi-year prepay
- Standard payment terms: Net 30

You mentioned procurement prefers Net90 for finance approval if we split payments across milestones. We'd like to understand what credit or security instrument AcmeCloud would provide to cover the early-service exposure. Two options we can pursue: (A) a signed credit letter / bank guarantee, or (B) move more dollars upfront (50%) and reduce Net terms on the remainder.

I've attached a one-page credit-letter template (for your review) and the Commitment Schedule v3. If you can confirm which direction procurement wants to go I can loop in Finance and Legal and draft the final redlines.

Next steps: can we lock demo + procurement call next Tue (Oct 5) to finalize?

Thanks,

Laura Bennett

Laura —

Thanks for sending. High level this looks good and the discount is attractive. A few asks from our side before we route to finance: 

- Can Redwood accept Net90 on the milestone invoices? Our standard for multi-year commitments is Net90 for anything processed through our centralized AP.
- If Net90 is non-starter, can you confirm the credit letter approach and whether Redwood will accept a corporate letter of credit from our bank (we typically provide a standby LC) or a parent guarantee.
- We need clearer milestone acceptance criteria (what constitutes achieved usage band) — can your team add objective telemetry thresholds so acceptance is unambiguous?

We are targeting an internal procurement review next Wed (Oct 6). If you can provide finance-ready language and an updated SOW with the telemetry thresholds, we can expedite.

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers below and next steps: 

- Net90: Redwood can accommodate Net90 on milestone invoices conditional on one of the following being in place: (1) a bank standby LC for the outstanding milestone amount, or (2) a signed credit letter plus an initial larger upfront payment (we typically ask for 30% upfront).
- Credit instruments: We accept a bank-issued standby Letter of Credit or a corporate guarantee. The attached CreditLetter-Redwood-template is our preferred minimum wording for a corporate letter. If you're providing an LC we can share bank details via secure channel.
- Milestone telemetry: noted — looping in Aditya (SE) to draft objective thresholds (API call volumes, sustained concurrency, or spend windows).

If that sounds acceptable I'll ask Finance and Legal to prep the contract language and a short amendment for Net90 on covered milestone invoices. Otherwise, if procurement prefers to avoid external credit instruments we can increase upfront to 50% and then use Net30 on the remainder.

I'll hold a slot for Tue Oct 5 at 10am PT for the procurement call — please confirm.

Janet / Laura —

Following up from Finance: Redwood is willing to provide a signed credit letter and accept a standby LC for milestone invoicing, subject to standard KYC and bank confirmation. Practical proposal from our side to bridge procurement comfort: 

1) Payment split: 30% upfront at signature (covers initial ramp and capacity reservation)
2) Milestones: remaining 70% billed in four equal milestone invoices annually (7 milestones total over 3 years) with Net90 payment terms on each milestone invoice
3) Security: Acme provides a bank standby Letter of Credit to cover outstanding milestone amounts OR executes Redwood's corporate credit letter (attached) to be returned at signature.
4) Early termination: any unbilled prepaid credit is refundable on a declining schedule (see Commitment schedule).

We understand LC processing can add time — if that materially delays the deal we will accept a 50% upfront alternative and Net30 on remainder as Laura suggested.

If procurement wants a version of the credit letter with Acme's legal language we can redline. We'll also add standardized acceptance metrics for each milestone: e.g., monthly invoice tied to 30-day rolling usage thresholds or explicit API-concurrency gates.

-Markus Klein

Hi Janet — looping in as requested. Below are draft objective telemetry thresholds we propose for milestone acceptance (we can surface these in the SOW table):

- Milestone A (initial ramp): average monthly token consumption >= 150k tokens for a consecutive 30-day window OR sustained 50 concurrent active requests for 7 straight days
- Milestone B/C (scale phases): aggregated spend for the milestone period >= $225k (per milestone) OR API QPS consistently >= X for 14 days (we'll set QPS after a short ramp discovery)
- Failure to meet telemetry: milestone is considered unmet and billing will be deferred until thresholds are achieved for the next billing window; Redwood will provide usage reports and a 72-hour support window for dispute resolution.

If this looks reasonable we can bake into SOW-Attachment.xlsx and send a finance-ready doc for your procurement review.

Thanks,
